sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and honesty rules
sections.what: Brings in the chart's point type and states the rules this adapter follows: plot only complete points, never fake sizes, and never guess stages.
sections.why: The comments explain why the rules exist. They are the main safety guide for this file.
sections.watch_out: Any change to this file must keep these rules, or the chart will show misleading points.

sections.name: ScanFieldRecord
sections.title: One field record shape
sections.what: Describes one field's record: its value, verification status, whether it was calculated or approximated, where it came from, and why it is missing if it is.
sections.why: The comment says this copies the server's contract by hand, because the client does not import server code.
sections.watch_out: It must be updated by hand whenever the server's record changes.

sections.name: ScanProjectResult
sections.title: One project result shape
sections.what: Describes one project's ID, name, industry and its map of fields.
sections.why: Matches the project entries in the finalize result.
sections.watch_out: Any field may be missing, so lookups can return nothing.

sections.name: ScanRunResult
sections.title: Whole run result shape
sections.what: Describes the stored finalize result: a version number, all projects, and the totals.
sections.why: Describes the saved summary that this adapter reads.
sections.watch_out: The version number is stored but nothing here checks it, so an unexpected version would not be flagged.

sections.name: num
sections.title: Safe number conversion
sections.what: Turns a value into a number, or nothing if the value is missing or not a usable number.
sections.why: Prevents missing values from being treated as real numbers.
sections.watch_out: An empty or blank text value becomes zero here, not nothing, because of how the conversion works.

sections.name: str
sections.title: Safe text conversion
sections.what: Keeps a text value only when it has visible characters after trimming spaces, and returns nothing otherwise.
sections.why: Stops blank labels from appearing on the chart.
sections.watch_out: Numbers are rejected here, so a numeric code stored as a number would be dropped.

sections.name: scanNaReasons
sections.title: Reasons a project is off the chart
sections.what: Lists, in plain text, why the cost deviation or the schedule overrun is not available for a project.
sections.why: Lets the user see the reason a project is missing from the chart.
sections.watch_out: If no reason was stored, the text says not computed, which does not explain why.

sections.name: derivedTrusted
sections.title: Trust check for a calculated figure
sections.what: Decides whether a figure can be trusted. It is trusted if it was reported directly, or if every input it was calculated from was verified.
sections.why: The comment explains the rule: directly reported figures are already in the source, and calculated ones need verified inputs.
sections.watch_out: The input field names are fixed in the code, so a renamed field makes the figure look untrusted without any error.

sections.name: scanInputQuality
sections.title: Solid or dimmed bubble
sections.what: Marks a project solid when both its cost and schedule figures are trusted, and dimmed otherwise.
sections.why: The comment says the dimmed style warns the user that inputs were not fully verified.
sections.watch_out: One untrusted axis dims the whole bubble.

sections.name: toBubblePoint
sections.title: Building the bubble point
sections.what: Builds the chart point: horizontal position is delay in years, vertical position is cost deviation, and size comes from planned budget or capacity. It also fills in name, stage, country, technology and contractor, and marks approximate delays using true or false values.
sections.why: Converts the scan result into the shape the shared chart expects.
sections.watch_out: Delay is divided by twelve to get years, so the delay must be in months. The approximation check uses true or false fields, not text.

summary: Converts one finished project result into a point for the cost and schedule bubble chart, and returns nothing when showing that point would be misleading.
purpose: Lets the shared bubble chart show Reality Scan results without inventing or filling in numbers.
why: The top-of-file comments state honesty rules: plot only when both axes exist, never fake a size, and never guess a lifecycle stage.
how: It reads the finalize result for one project. It checks that cost deviation and schedule overrun both have values. It picks the bubble size from planned budget or capacity, depending on the chosen mode. It marks the point as approximate when the source says so, and builds the labels for name, country, technology and contractor. Two helpers explain why a project is off the chart and whether its inputs are trusted, which decides between a solid and a dimmed bubble.
inputs: One project result from the finalize stage, and the size mode, either CAPEX or CAPACITY.
outputs: A bubble point or nothing, a list of reasons a project is off the chart, and a solid or dimmed label.
risks: A size of zero or a missing budget or capacity leaves the bubble without a size. The field names for schedule overrun and delay are used in more than one place. A renamed input field silently makes results look untrusted.
debug: If a project is missing from the chart, call the reasons helper on its result to see why. If a bubble has no size, check the planned budget or capacity values and the chosen mode. If a bubble looks faded, check the verification status of its inputs.
